posts.author: Aleth728
posts.body:
Apu's Journey is an action-rpg made in the RPG Maker MV engine, you can complete dungeons, defeat creatures, collect items and improve your skills!
Apu decides to start a journey, although a strange feeling hovers in his heart. After encountering a strange figure, something happens... It's up to Apu to destroy the three seal masks and prevent evil from returning to our world.
A mix of puzzles, action, adventure and exploration based on games like The Legend of Zelda;
Art style based on classic Game boy games with monochromatic palettes;
Possibility to unlock a large number of achievements,
Choose the difficulty mode that makes you feel most comfortable, whether you are a casual player or looking for a great challenge, among other features.

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I gave your demo a try. I ended up quitting during the mine dungeon because the gameplay just isn't for me, but I think you've done a pretty good job matching the older Legend of Zelda vibes.
Spoiler:
Feedback
I'll start with something I really enjoyed, which is the art style you chose. It's very cute and works well together, and the full CGs that show up once in a while are great. The story seems interesting, even if I didn't get to see tons of it, so I would've liked to play more if I wasn't horrendous at the gameplay.
On-map battles are difficult in RPG Maker, and unfortunately this game suffers from that clunkiness. Not being able to turn in place makes it harder to line up next to enemies, so I had to run around the map to try to avoid enemies while also getting into a good spot to attack them. Apu's sword attack range felt really small, especially when I'd finally get lined up and then the enemy moves so they were diagonal from Apu... I don't know if it would make the game too easy, but having the sword strike three spaces wide instead of just one would have saved me so much headache in combat.
One of the main reasons I gave up was the lack of healing. I don't know if it's my terrible RNG luck or the game, but I rarely got hearts out of pots so I kept dying over and over. It wasn't that the enemies were too strong, I just couldn't get positioned right to safely attack without getting hit once or twice a map. You may want to double-check the chances of them dropping, and increase it if your player is dying and respawning often. The fact the hearts only healed one health piece also made it harder, it would have been nice to have some that healed half a heart or even very rarely a full heart.
As I mentioned, I quit in the mines. The bats just flew too quickly for me to kill them before they'd hit me two or three times, and I kept getting trapped in doorways by them so I couldn't run back to the entrance to save and go buy healing items. Another player may have an easier time there, but I just couldn't get the timing right.
There were also some small bugs and oddities:
Can't turn sound off fully in the Setting menu
The item info "Info: ???" is blurry in the inventory
Consider adding a Settings option to turn off the zoom in when moving between rooms, it's a bit disorienting
Can be attacked in the Inventory, do you not want players to be able to pause?
The large slime boss can be walked into and behind, making it hard to see Apu
Why is the Compass in the normal menu, when the peddler sells from a custom menu?
Having a map of the Mushroom Forest is nice, but it doesn't show where the exits in each map are so it's not as helpful as it could be
Jintrock (I think that's how you spell his name) has a skill where he sits on the ground and summons flames that shoot across the screen, but they only showed up at the top and the bottom of the screen so it wasn't a danger
After getting the item that draws coins to me, pots that are being destroyed also draw closer to Apu
Overall, this seems promising, it's just not a game for me. I do think polishing the controls and settings more will make playing more enjoyable for fans of this type of game, so consider tweaking some of that.
Good luck with your project!

Artille
posts.body:
First impressions : DAMN
It looks really polished (I encountered 1 glitch and 1 maybe reset issue so far, but that's about it)
The story so far is typical of old school rpg's
The combat mechanic is a bit stiff, but you get used to it pretty fast
The overall flow is great honestly
The music is pretty nice too
The glitch I encountered was the first death, the SE played twice
Only happened on the first death, did not happen since.
The reset issue I found was in the (first?) dungeon part, just before the 3 moving blocks, two pots gave me quarter of a heart (playing a green exclamation icon)
However, when I died and came back to that place, no quarter heart where found (maybe its RNG based though, so uncertain)
Great work so far! I like it.

posts.body:
Hey, merci,
@Artille
. How's it going? I received feedback from someone who really enjoyed the game, and I'm happy about that. I hope you continue enjoying the gameplay. Feel free to report any issues you encounter.
The first problem you reported about the music stopping and not returning has been properly fixed; it was an oversight on my part after updating the maps. The second error was also fixed. I ended up using the same picture ID for items and the save notification, which caused the weird issue.
You really lifted my spirits with your impressions and helped me even more by reporting the small issues you found! I hope you can reach 100% while having fun in Apu's universe! I'll be uploading updates along with the fixes you pointed out soon. Cheers!
